<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"
align=center><B>PART I</B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>ITEM
1. &nbsp;DESCRIPTION OF BUSINESS</B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B><U>History</U></B></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>We were incorporated under the laws of the State of Idaho as
Superior Mines Company on January 22, 1962. &nbsp;We were established for the
purposes of mineral exploration in the state of Idaho and Montana. &nbsp;In 1964
our name was changed to Superior Silver Mines, Inc. &nbsp;The Company has been
dormant for a number of years. &nbsp;It currently holds one unpatented mineral
claim. &nbsp;There are no known mineral reserves on the Company&#146;s property.
&nbsp;Due to the increase in the price of gold, silver and other metals over the
past several years, management is reactivating the Company with the intention of
investigating opportunities in the natural resource industry. Because we have no
operations and only nominal assets we are what the Securities and Exchange
Commission &nbsp;defines as &nbsp;a shell company. At such time as we cease to
be a shell company we will need to file a Form 8-K that contains the information
that would be required in an initial registration statement on Form 10 or Form
10SB to register a class of securities under Section 12 of the Securities
Exchange Act of 1934. We will be required to file the Form 8-K within four
business days after the closing of the transaction that results in our no longer
being considered a shell company</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>We are registering its shares under the Securities Exchange Act of
1934 (the &#147;Exchange Act&#148;) for the purpose of becoming a reporting company.
&nbsp;The Company believes that it will be better able to finance its operations
if it is a reporting company. &nbsp;Management believes the benefits of becoming
a reporting company include the ability to obtain support of market makers,
facilitating or improving the terms on which additional equity financing may be
sought, providing liquidity for stock options or similar benefits to key
employees, and providing liquidity for all shareholders by qualifying to list on
the NASDAQ supervised OTC Bulletin Board. </P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px"><B>Risk Factors</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>The Company&#146;s business is subject to numerous risk factors,
including the following: </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 36px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;&nbsp; <FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&nbsp;Because
the Company was historically engaged in the mineral exploration industry, there
exists the possibility that the Company may have environmental liability.
&nbsp;Management has no knowledge of any actions of the Company that might give
rise to such potential liability, but there can be no assurance that the Company
may not at some future date be deemed to have environmental
liabilities.</FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp; The
Company has had no revenues or earnings from operations. The Company has no
significant assets or financial resources. &nbsp;As a mineral exploration
company, the Company will sustain operating expenses without corresponding
revenues. &nbsp;This will result in the Company incurring net operating losses
that will increase continuously until the Company can bring a property into
production or lease, joint venture or sell any property it may
acquire.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>2</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"> Mineral exploration
and development are highly speculative and capital intensive. &nbsp;Most
exploration efforts are not successful in that they do not result in the
discovery of mineralization of sufficient quantity or quality to be profitably
mined. &nbsp;The operations of the Company are also indirectly subject to all of
the hazards and risks normally incident to developing and operating mining
properties. &nbsp;These risks include insufficient ore reserves; fluctuations in
production costs that may make mining of reserves uneconomic; significant
environmental and other regulatory restrictions; labor disputes; geological
problems; failure of pit walls or dams; </FONT><FONT
style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><I>force majeure</I></FONT><FONT
style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"> events; and the risk of injury to persons,
property or the environment.</FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Courier New"
align=justify>o<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&nbsp; Our property
does not contain any reserves. The probability of an individual prospect ever
having reserves is remote. &nbsp;As such, any funds spent on exploration could
be lost which will result in a loss of your investment. Even if we were ever to
develop reserves, ore reserve figures and costs are primarily estimates and are
not guarantees of recovery of the indicated quantities of these metals.
&nbsp;There are numerous uncertainties inherent in estimating proven and
probable reserves and mineralization, including many factors beyond the control
of the Company. &nbsp;The estimation of reserves and mineralization is a
subjective process, and the accuracy of any such estimates is a function of the
quality of available data and of engineering and geological interpretation and
judgment. &nbsp;Results of drilling, metallurgical testing and production and
the evaluation of mine plans subsequent to the date of any estimate may justify
revision of such estimates. &nbsp;No assurance can be given that the estimate of
the amount of metal or the indicated level of recovery of these metals will be
realized. &nbsp;Reserve estimates for properties that have not yet started
production may change based on actual production experience. &nbsp;Further,
reserves are valued based on estimates of costs and metals prices. The economic
value of ore reserves may be adversely affected by:</FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 136px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Courier New"
align=justify>o<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"> declines in the
market price of the various metals we mine; </FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 136px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Courier New"
align=justify>o<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"> increased production
or capital costs; or </FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 136px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Courier New"
align=justify>o<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"> recovery rates.
</FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>Assumptions about prices are subject to greater uncertainty, and
metals prices have fluctuated widely in the past. &nbsp;Declines in the market
price of base or precious metals also may render reserves or mineralization
containing relatively lower grades of ore uneconomic to exploit. &nbsp;Changes
in operating and capital costs and other factors including, but not limited to,
short-term operating factors such as the need for sequential development of
orebodies and the processing of new or different ore grades may materially and
adversely affect reserves. &nbsp;However, if the price of metals declines
substantially below the levels used to calculate reserves for an extended
period, we could experience: </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 136px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Courier New"
align=justify>o<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"> delays in new project
development; </FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 136px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Courier New"
align=justify>o<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"> increased net losses;
</FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 136px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Courier New"
align=justify>o<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"> reduced cash flow;
</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>3</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 136px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Courier New"
align=justify>o<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"> reductions in
reserves; and </FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 136px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Courier New"
align=justify>o<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"> write-down of asset
values.</FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&nbsp; The
profitability of mining operations is directly related to the market price of
the metals being mined. &nbsp;The market price of base and precious metals such
as copper, silver and gold fluctuate widely and is affected by numerous factors
beyond the control of any mining company. &nbsp;These factors include
expectations with respect to the rate of inflation, the exchange rates of the
dollar and other currencies, interest rates, global or regional political,
economic or banking crises, and a number of other factors. &nbsp;If the market
price of silver or copper should drop dramatically, the value of the Company&#146;s
exploration properties could also drop dramatically; and the Company might not
be able to recover its investment in those properties. &nbsp;The selection of a
property for exploration or development, the determination to construct a mine
and place it into production, and the dedication of funds necessary to achieve
such purposes are decisions that must be made long before the first revenues
from production will be received. &nbsp;Price fluctuations between the time that
such decisions are made and the commencement of production can drastically
affect the economics of a mine.</FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"> Our business is
subject to extensive federal, state and local laws and regulations governing
development, production, labor standards, occupational health, waste disposal,
use of toxic substances, environmental regulations, mine safety and other
matters. &nbsp;New legislation and regulations may be adopted at any time that
results in additional operating expense, capital expenditures or restrictions
and delays in the mining, production or development of our properties.
&nbsp;Various laws and permits require that financial assurances be in place for
certain environmental and reclamation obligations and other potential
liabilities. &nbsp;The amount of the financial assurances and the amount
required to be set aside by us as collateral for these financial assurances will
be dependent upon a number of factors, including our financial condition,
reclamation cost estimates, development of new projects and the total dollar
value of financial assurances in place.</FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&nbsp; We compete with
other mineral exploration and mining companies, almost all of which have greater
financial resources than us or are further in their development, for the
acquisition of mineral claims, leases and other mineral interests as well as for
the recruitment and retention of qualified employees and other personnel.
&nbsp;If we require and are unsuccessful in acquiring additional mineral
properties or personnel, we will not be able to grow at the rate we desire, or
at all.</FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&nbsp; You should not
rely on an investment in our common stock to provide dividend income, as we do
not plan to pay cash dividends on our common stock in the foreseeable future.
</FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&nbsp; Our common
stock is quoted on the Pink Sheets. &nbsp;Trading in stock quoted in the Pink
Sheets is often thin and characterized by wide fluctuations in trading prices
due to many factors that may have little to do with our operations or business
prospects. &nbsp;This volatility could depress the market price of our common
stock for reasons unrelated to operating performance. &nbsp;Moreover, the Pink
Sheets is not a stock exchange, and trading of securities on the Pink Sheets is
often more sporadic than the trading of securities listed on a quotation system
or a stock exchange such as the Amex. &nbsp;Accordingly, shareholders may have
difficulty reselling any of the shares.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>4</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&nbsp; One of our
directors, Terrence Dunne served as the Chief Financial Officer and a Director
for Daybreak Oil and Gas, Inc. (Daybreak) from April 2006 until December , 2007.
During Mr. Dunne&#146;s tenure with Daybreak, the Company experienced two delinquent
filings. The Form 10-QSB for the fiscal quarter ended November 30, 2006 and the
Form 10-KSB for the fiscal year ended February 28, 2007 were filed subsequent to
their statutory due dates.</FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>The filings were delinquent due to management&#146;s decision (which
included Mr. Dunne) to restate previously filed financial statements. The
restated financial statements included the four (4) quarters for the fiscal year
ended February 28, 2006 and the first three (3) quarters for the fiscal year
ended February 28, 2007. The decision to restate these financial periods was in
response to comments of the SEC staff in connection with the submission of a
registration statement. These comments involved the Commission&#146;s interpretation
of recently enacted accounting standards concerning the valuation of stock based
compensation. The decision to restate the financial statements was predicated on
the pre-effective application of newly enacted accounting standards. The
Company's management conferred with the Company's audit committee and the
Company's independent public accounting firm to arrive at this decision </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&nbsp; Our stock is a
penny stock. &nbsp;The Securities and Exchange Commission has adopted Rule 15g-9
which generally defines &#147;penny stock&#148; to be any equity security that has a
market price (as defined) less than $5.00 per share or an exercise price of less
than $5.00 per share, subject to certain exceptions. &nbsp;Our securities are
covered by the penny stock rules which impose additional sales practice
requirements on broker-dealers who sell to persons other than established
customers and &#147;accredited investors.&#148; &nbsp;The term &#147;accredited investor&#148;
refers generally to institutions with assets in excess of $5,000,000 or
individuals with a net worth in excess of $1,000,000 or annual income exceeding
$200,000 individually or $300,000 jointly with their spouse. &nbsp;The penny
stock rules require a broker-dealer, prior to a transaction in a penny stock not
otherwise exempt from the rules, to deliver a standardized risk disclosure
document in a form prepared by the SEC which provides information about penny
stocks and the nature and level of risks in the penny stock market. &nbsp;The
broker-dealer also must provide the customer with current bid and offer
quotations for the penny stock, the compensation of the broker-dealer and its
salesperson in the transaction, and monthly account statements showing the
market value of each penny stock held in the customer&#146;s account. &nbsp;The bid
and offer quotations and the broker-dealer and salesperson compensation
information must be given to the customer orally or in writing prior to
effecting the transaction and must be given to the customer in writing before or
with the customer&#146;s confirmation. &nbsp;In addition, the penny stock rules
require that, prior to a transaction in a penny stock not otherwise exempt from
these rules, the broker-dealer must make a special written determination that
the penny stock is a suitable investment for the purchaser and receive the
purchaser&#146;s written agreement to the transaction. &nbsp;These disclosure
requirements may have the effect of reducing the level of trading activity in
the secondary market for the stock that is subject to these penny stock rules.
&nbsp;Consequently, these penny stock rules may affect the ability of
broker-dealers to trade our securities. &nbsp;We believe that the penny stock
rules discourage investor interest in and limit the marketability of our common
stock.</FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>In addition to the &#147;penny stock&#148; rules promulgated by the
Securities and Exchange Commission, the NASD has adopted rules that require, in
recommending an investment to a customer, a broker-dealer must have reasonable
grounds for believing that the investment is suitable for that customer.
&nbsp;Prior to recommending speculative, low-priced securities to their </P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>5</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always"
align=justify>non-institutional customers, broker-dealers must make reasonable
efforts to obtain information about the customer&#146;s financial status, tax status,
investment objectives and other information. &nbsp;Under interpretations of
these rules, the NASD believes there is a high probability that speculative,
low-priced securities will not be suitable for at least some customers.
&nbsp;The NASD requirements make it more difficult for broker-dealers to
recommend that their customers buy our common stock, which may limit your
ability to buy and sell our stock. </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify> &#183;&nbsp;
<FONT
style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"> Because the Company is a shell company,
shareholders holding unregistered shares of the Company&#146;s common stock will not
be able to avail themselves of Rule 144 for the resale of such restricted
securities.
</FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify> &#183;&nbsp;
<FONT
style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"> Restrictions on the resale of restricted
shares of the Company&#146;s common stock due to its shell company status may make it
difficult, more expensive or impossible for the Company to finance any business
opportunity.
</FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify> &#183;&nbsp;
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"> The
Company will be required to file current &#147;Form 10 information&#148; with the
Securities and Exchange Commission within four days of any business acquisition.
This may increase the cost of such an acquisition or preclude some business
opportunities entirely.
</FONT></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify> &#183;&nbsp;
<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"> Until
such time as the Company ceases to be shell Company it will be required to
comply with Rule 419 under the Securities Act of 1933. This rule governs the
offering of securities by &#147;blank check&#148; companies. Our Company is deemed to be a
&#147;blank check&#148; because it is a development stage company that has no specific
business plan or purpose or has indicated that its business plan is to engage in
a merger or acquisition with an unidentified company or companies, or other
entity or person, and is issuing &#147;penny stock.&#148; Rule 419 imposes additional
requirements on a blank check company which seeks to offer its securities .
Compliance with Rule 419 may make any such contemplated offering more expensive
to the Company, more difficult to find potential investors and more time
consuming to effect a business transaction. Such requirements include the escrow
of the proceeds of any offering, the obligation of the Company to provide, and
the right of the purchaser to receive, information regarding an acquisition,
including the requirement that purchasers confirm in writing their investment in
the Company after an acquisition candidate is identified and the probable
requirement of a post-effective amendment to the offering document setting forth
information about the acquisition target &nbsp;that would be required in the
applicable form of registration statement. Compliance with Rule 419 will
increase the cost of any such offering, may make investment in the Company less
attractive to certain investors and may make the Company less attractive to
potential acquisition candidates.
</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px"><B><U>Employees</U></B></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>We currently have no employees. &nbsp;We intend to utilize the
services of outside consultants and contractors to provide additional services
to the Company.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B><U>Competition</U></B></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>There is aggressive competition within the minerals industry to
discover and acquire properties considered to have commercial potential.
&nbsp;The Company competes for the opportunity to participate in promising
exploration projects with other entities, many of which have greater </P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>6</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always"
align=justify>resources than the Company. &nbsp;In addition, the Company
competes with others in efforts to obtain financing to explore and develop
mineral properties.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B><U>Regulation</U></B></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>The Company&#146;s activities in the United States are subject to
various federal, state, and local laws and regulations governing prospecting,
development, production, labor standards, occupational health and mine safety,
control of toxic substances, and other matters involving environmental
protection and taxation. &nbsp;It is possible that future changes in these laws
or regulations could have a significant impact on the Company&#146;s business,
causing those activities to be economically reevaluated at that time.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>ITEM
2. MANAGEMENT&#146;S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF
OPERATIONS</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify> Superior Silver Mines, Inc. (&#147;the Company&#148;) was established in
1962 for the purpose of mineral exploration, but has been dormant for a number
of years. Due to the increase in the price of gold, silver and other metals,
management is reactivating the Company with the intention of investigating
opportunities in the natural resource industry. However, the Company will not
restrict its search to any specific business or industry, and the Company may
participate in a business venture of virtually any kind or nature.
</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt" align=justify> The
Company seeks to investigate and, if such investigation warrants, acquire an
interest in a business seeking the perceived advantages of a publicly registered
corporation. &nbsp;The Company may seek a business opportunity with an entity
which has recently commenced operations, wishes to utilize the public
marketplace in order to raise additional capital to expand into new products or
markets, develop a new product or service, or for other corporate purposes.
&nbsp;The Company may acquire assets and/or establish subsidiaries in various
businesses, or acquire existing businesses as subsidiaries. &nbsp;Business
opportunities may be available in many different industries at various stages of
development, all of which will make the task of comparative investigation and
analysis of such business opportunities extremely difficult and complex.

</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 12pt" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; LINE-HEIGHT: 14pt"
align=justify> Management of the Company, while not especially experienced in
matters relating to the new direction of the Company, will rely primarily upon
their own efforts to accomplish the business purposes. &nbsp;The Company does
not anticipate a significant change in the number of employees during the next
12 months. It is not anticipated that any outside consultants or advisors, other
than the Company's legal counsel, will be utilized to effectuate its business
purposes described herein. During the next twelve months, the Company expects to
be able to satisfy its cash requirements, and does not foresee the need to raise
additional capital during this period.
</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>The Company is voluntarily registering its common stock under the
Securities Exchange Act of 1934. &nbsp;After completion of this registration, it
is the Company&#146;s intention to obtain a listing on the NASDAQ Supervised OTC
Bulletin Board. &nbsp;The Company believes that listing on the OTCBB will
facilitate the Company&#146;s efforts to obtain additional equity financing.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>7</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; MARGIN: 0px"><B>Year ended
December 31, 2007 compared to year ended December 31, 2006.</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px"><I>Result of Operations</I></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>During 2007, the Company&#146;s
only revenue was interest income in the amount of $2,832. &nbsp;This represents
a increase in income of $2,832 over the year ended December 31, 2006. This
increase is due to the fact that the Company had $360,833 more cash on hand
during the year ended December 31, 2007 than during the year ended December 31,
2006 due to an increase of cash and cash equivalents from the proceeds of
&nbsp;a private placement of the Company&#146;s common stock.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>Total expenses increased
from $18,921 in 2006 to $48,457 in 2007. &nbsp;The increase is primarily due to
the legal and accounting fees of approximately $34,000. Both of these items were
due to the Company&#146;s private placement of common stock and expenses incurred in
connection with the filing of a registration statement on Form 10 under the
Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended. In addition, general and
administrative expenses of 13,585 in 2007 &nbsp;contributed to the Company&#146;s
increased operating expenses although this was offset in part by $11,200 of
management and consulting expenses incurred 2006 which did not recur in
2007<FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 10pt">. &nbsp;</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px">As a result, the Company recorded a net
loss of $45,625 in 2007, compared to a net loss of $18,921 in 2006.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px"><I>Liquidity and Capital
Resources</I></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><I>Working Capital, Cash
and Cash Equivalents</I></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>The Company&#146;s positive
working capital at December 31, 2007 was $365,015 compared to positive working
capital of $9,255 at December 31, 2006. The ratio of current assets to current
liabilities was 39.06 to 1 at December 31, 2007 compared to 3.06 to 1 at
December 2006. Working capital increased in 2007 primarily due to the Company&#146;s
&nbsp;private placement of common stock in 2007. </P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>Net cash used in operating
activities was $40,530 in 2007 compared with $3,226 used in operating activities
in 2006. &nbsp;The increase is the result of the increased net loss from
operations because the company was substantially dormant in 2006.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>Cash flow from financing
activities was $401,385 in 2007 compared to $13,800 in 2006. &nbsp;The increase
is primarily the result of $360,095 received from the issuance of common stock
in a private placement and 41,300 received from the issuance of common stock
from the issuance of outatanding warrants.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>As a result, cash and cash
equivalents increased by $360,833 in 2007. &nbsp;The Company has cash and cash
equivalents of $374,605 as of December 31, 2007. &nbsp;It will not be necessary
for the Company to raise additional capital to continue it business activities
in 2008.</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 6px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6px"
align=justify><I>Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements</I></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 6px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 6px"
align=justify>There are no preliminary agreements or understandings between the
Company and its officers and directors or affiliates or lending institutions
with respect to any loan agreements. </P>
<P style="MARGIN: 6px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>8</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>

<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>ITEM
3. DESCRIPTION OF PROPERTY</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>We currently hold one

property and we do not intend to conduct any exploration activities on the
property</P>

<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify><B><U>Thomas S. Smith</U></B> has been a Director and the
President of the Company for more than the past fifteen years. &nbsp;Mr. Smith
has been engaged in the private practice of law for more than the past five
years. &nbsp;Mr. Smith received his Bachelor of Business degree from the
University of Idaho and his Juris Doctorate from Gonzaga University. &nbsp;Mr.
Smith serves as the president and a director of Nevada Stewart Mining Company, a
director of Highland Surprise Mining Company, and the Secretary/treasurer of
Homestake Silver and Lead Mining Company, all of which are non-reporting public
companies.</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify><B><U>H. James Magnuson</U></B> has been a Director and
Vice-President of the Company since June 2006. &nbsp;Since 1979, Mr. Magnuson
has been an attorney engaged in the private practice of Law in Coeur d&#146;Alene,
Idaho. Mr. Magnuson received his Bachelor of Science degree from the University
of Idaho and is graduated from Boston College with a Juris Doctorate.</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify><B><U>Dennis O&#146;Brien, CPA</U></B> has been the Secretary of the
Company since 2002 and its Principal Financial Officer since 2007. &nbsp;Since
1990, Mr. O&#146;Brien has been the accountant for H .F. Magnuson &amp; Company in
Wallace, Idaho. &nbsp;Mr. O&#146;Brien is graduated from Northern Illinois University
with a Bachelor of Science degree with a major in accounting. &nbsp;Mr. O&#146;Brien
serves as a director and secretary of numerous non-reporting public
companies.</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify><B><U>Terrence J. Dunne</U></B> has been a Director of the Company
since June 2006. &nbsp;For approximately the last five years, Mr. Dunne has
operated as a business consultant through his company Terrence J. Dunne &amp;
Associates. &nbsp;Mr. Dunne is graduated with a Bachelor of Business degree, a
Master&#146;s of Business and a Master&#146;s in Taxation all from Gonzaga University.
&nbsp;Mr. Dunne served as the </P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>10</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>

<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always"
align=justify>chief financial officer (4/06 &#150; 12/07) and as a director (1/06 &#150;
12/07) of Daybreak Oil &amp; Gas, Inc.; as chief financial officer (2006-01/08)
and as a director (2006- present) of Gold Crest Mines, Inc.; and as president(
2006-2007) director (director 2006 &#150; present) of Rock Energy Resources, Inc
(formerly Hanover Gold Company).</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify><B><U>Arthur P. Dammarell</U></B> has been a Director of the
Company since June 2006. &nbsp;From 2000 through March 2006, Mr. Dammarell was
the principal financial officer of Nova Oil, Inc. (now Nova Biosource Fuels,
Inc.). &nbsp;Mr. Dammarell is graduated from Eastern Washington University with
a Bachelor of Arts degree in Urban and Regional Planning.</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify><B><U>Dale B. Lavigne</U></B> has been a Director of the Company
since June 2006. &nbsp;Mr. Lavigne is graduated from the University of Montana
with a Bachelor of Science degree in Pharmacy. &nbsp;For the past 47 years, Mr.
Lavigne has been the Chairman and a Director of the Osburn Drug Company, Inc.; a
4-store chain of drug stores in North Idaho. &nbsp;Mr. Lavigne has been a
director of Daybreak Oil and Gas, Inc., <FONT style="FONT-SIZE: 11pt">since 1965
and served as the Company&#146;s President from 1989 until December 2004.
&nbsp;&nbsp;</FONT>Mr. Lavigne is the former Chairman of the First National Bank
of North Idaho, a former member of the Gonzaga University Board of Regents,
former President of the Silver Valley Economic Development Corporation, and a
current member of the Governor&#146;s Task Force on Rural Idaho.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>Director
Independence</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>Messrs. Dunne, Dammerall and Lavigne are independent members of
the board of directors and the audit committee as defined by NASDAQ Marketplace
Rules 4200(a)(15) and 4350(d)(2) respectively. </P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>In determining the matter of independence, neither Messrs. Messrs.
Dunne, Dammerall nor Lavigne had any transactions, relationships or arrangements
with the Company prior to or after becoming directors of the Company except for
becoming shareholders of the Company pursuant their investment participation in
the Company&#146;s private placements on the same terms as all other investors in
that offering. &nbsp;In determining the matter of director independence, the
following matrix was utilized.</P>

three years was, employed by the company or by any parent or subsidiary of the
company;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px">(2) a director who accepted or who has a Family Member
who accepted any compensation from the company .&nbsp;.&nbsp;. in excess of
$60,000 during any period of twelve consecutive months within the three years
preceding the determination of independence, other than the following: </P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 72px; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -48px">(i) compensation
for board or board committee service;</P>

<P
style="PADDING-LEFT: 72px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -48px">(ii)
compensation paid to a Family Member who is an employee (other than an executive
officer) of the company ; or</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 72px; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -48px">(iii) benefits
under a tax-qualified retirement plan, or non-discretionary compensation</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 5px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px">(3) Other relationships
include:</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 5px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px">(i) a
director who is a Family Member of an individual who is, or at any time during
the past three years was, employed by the Company or by any parent or subsidiary
of the Company made, or from which the Company received, payments for property
or services in the current or any of the past three fiscal years that exceed 5%
of the recipient's consolidated gross revenues for that year, or $200,000,
whichever is more, other than (i) payments arising solely from investments in
the company's securities; or(ii) payments under non-discretionary charitable
contribution matching programs.</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 5px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px">(ii) a
director of the Company who is, or has a Family Member who is, employed as an
executive officer of another entity where at any time during the past three
years any of the executive officers of the Company serve on the compensation
committee of such other entity; or</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 6px; PADDING-LEFT: 24px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px">(iii) a
director who is, or has a Family Member who is, a current partner of the
Company's outside auditor, or was a partner or employee of the Company's outside
auditor who worked on the company's audit at any time during any of the past
three years.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>Board
Committees</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>The entire Board of Directors presently serves as our Audit,
Nominating and Compensation Committees and will continue to serve in such
capacity until said committees are established. &nbsp;We have not yet adopted a
Code of Ethics for our Executive Officers but intend to do so during the second
quarter of 2008.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>Conflicts
of Interest</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>Officers and Directors have a fiduciary duty to our shareholders
and owe the Company a duty to advance the Company&#146;s business interests when the
opportunity to do so arises. As a result, Officers and Directors are prohibited
from taking personal advantage of certain business opportunities in which the
Company may be interested. This so-called &#147;corporate opportunity doctrine&#148; is
complicated and it is not possible to clearly define all of the business
opportunities which belong or could be of interest to the Company and what
business opportunities may be taken advantage of personally by Officers or
Directors. The most common types of situations falling within this corporate
opportunity doctrine prohibit Officers and Directors from: (i) personally taking
advantage of any business opportunity that typically would be pursued by, or
would be of interest to, the Company; (ii) personally taking advantage of any
other business opportunity that the Company may want to take advantage of if the
opportunity is discovered using Company property, business contacts or
information, or that the Officer becomes aware of because he or she works for
the Company (or that a Director becomes aware of in his or her capacity as a
director of the Company).</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>Legal
Proceedings</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>No Director, or person nominated to become a Director or Executive
Officer, has been involved in any legal action involving the Company during the
past five years.</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>12</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>ITEM
6. EXECUTIVE COMPENSATION</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 13px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>None of our officers or directors receive any compensation for
serving in such position. In &nbsp;June 2007 we authorized the payment of
224,000 shares of our common stock to the Thomas S. Smith. This compensation
represented compensation for legal services performed by Mr. Smith over the
previous seven years. The shares were valued at $0.025 per share based upon
management&#146;s estimate of the fair value of the shares on the date of
issuance.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>ITEM
7. CERTAIN RELATIONSHIPS AND RELATED TRANSACTIONS AND DIRECTOR INDEPE</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>There have been no transactions or series of transactions, or
proposed transactions during the last two years to which the Registrant is a
party in which any Director, nominee for election as a Director, executive
officer or beneficial owner of five percent or more of the Registrant&#146;s common
stock, or any member of the immediate family of the foregoing had or is to have
a direct or indirect material interest exceeding $60,000.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>ITEM
8. DESCRIPTION OF SECURITIES</B></P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>COMMON
STOCK</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>We are authorized to issue five hundred million (500,000,000)
shares of $0.0001 par value common stock. &nbsp;All of the common stock
authorized has equal voting rights and powers without restrictions in
preference. &nbsp;All shares of common stock are equal to each other with
respect to voting, liquidation, dividend and other rights. &nbsp;Owners of
shares of common stock are entitled to one vote for each share of common stock
owned at any shareholders&#146; meeting. &nbsp;Holders of shares of common stock are
entitled to receive such dividends as may be declared by the Board of Directors
out of funds legally available therefor; and upon liquidation, are entitled to
participate pro rata in a distribution of assets available for such a
distribution to shareholders.</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>At June 30, 2008, there were 20,654,398 shares of common stock
issued and outstanding held by approximately 1,392 shareholders of record.
&nbsp;There are no outstanding options. </P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>PREFERRED
STOCK</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>We are authorized to issue 10,000,000 shares of Preferred Stock.
At December 11, 2007, there were no shares of preferred stock issued and
outstanding. &nbsp;The Preferred Stock is entitled to preference over the Common
Stock with respect to the distribution of assets of the Company in the event of
liquidation, dissolution, or winding-up of the Company, whether voluntarily or
involuntarily, or in the event of any other distribution of assets of the
Company among its shareholders for the purpose of winding-up its affairs.
&nbsp;The authorized but un-issued shares of Preferred Stock may be divided into
and issued in designated series from time to time by one or more resolutions
adopted by the Board of Directors. &nbsp;The Directors in their sole discretion
have the power to determine the preferences, limitations, and relative rights of
each series of Preferred Stock within the limits set forth in the Idaho Business
Corporations Act. &nbsp;As of the date of this memorandum, no preferred stock
has been issued.</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>There are no conversion, preemptive, or other subscription rights
or privileges with respect to any shares. &nbsp;Our stock does not have
cumulative voting rights, which means that the holders of more than fifty
percent (50%) of the shares voting in an election of directors may elect all of
the </P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>13</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always"
align=justify>directors if they choose to do so. &nbsp;In such event, the
holders of the remaining shares aggregating less than fifty percent (50%) would
not be able to elect any directors.</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify><B>Transfer Agent</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>We utilize the services of Columbia Stock Transfer Company, 601
East Seltice Way, Suite 202, Post Falls, Idaho 83854, as our transfer agent and
registrar. </P>

<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B><U>Dividends</U></B></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>We have never paid any dividends and does not anticipate the
payment of dividends in the foreseeable future.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>ITEM
2. LEGAL PROCEEDINGS</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>The Company is not a party to any legal proceedings, nor have any
judgments been taken, nor have any actions or suits been filed or threatened
against it or its Managers in their capacities as such, nor are the Officers and
Directors aware of any such claims that could give rise to such litigation.</P>

<P

3. CHANGES IN AND DISAGREEMENTS WITH ACCOUNTANTS</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>During the Company&#146;s two most recent fiscal years and subsequent
interim period, the principal accountant had not resigned (or declined to stand
for re-election) or was dismissed.</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"
align=justify>In addition, the Company&#146;s principal accountant had no
disagreements with the Company on any matter of Financial Reporting Policies and
Procedures.</P>
<P
style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman Bold"><B>ITEM
4. RECENT SALES OF UNREGISTERED SECURITIES</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>During December 2006, the
Company sold 552,000 shares of its unregistered common stock for $0.025 per
share. &nbsp;The proceeds to the Company from the sale were $13,800. &nbsp;The
shares were offered to and purchased by four individuals, each of whom was an
accredited investor. The purchasers consisted of three directors and one
executive officer of the Company. Management believes that the offering was
exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933 (&#147;the Act&#146;) pursuant
to Rule 506 of Regulation D and Section 4(2) of the Act. &nbsp;Proceeds from the
offering were used to fund the Company&#146;s general and administrative expenses.
All offers were made by the issued and no commissions were paid, directly or
indirectly, &nbsp;in connection with the offer and sale of the shares.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>During July and August
2007, the Company sold 10,325,000 shares of its unregistered common stock for
$0.04 per share. &nbsp;The shares were offered and sold only to accredited
investors as that term is defined in Regulation D. Commissions of $41,300 were
paid to underwriters in connection with the offering. These shares were issued
on September 13, 2007 and the proceeds to the Company from the offering were
$360,085. the names of the purchasers and the number of shares acquired and the
dollar amount invested are set forth as follows:</P>

<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>Management believes that
the offering was exempt from registration under the Securities Act of 1933 (&#147;the
Act&#146;) pursuant to Section 4(2) of the Act and Rule 506 of Regulation D.
&nbsp;Proceeds from the offering are expected to be used to fund the Company&#146;s
general and administrative expenses.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>During October 2007, the
Company sold 516,250 shares of its unregistered common stock for $0.08 per
share. &nbsp;This sale related to the exercise of all of the warrants received
by the Placement Agent in the July and August 2007 private placement. &nbsp;The
proceeds to the Company from the exercise were $41,300. Proceeds from the
exercise are expected to be used to fund the Company&#146;s general and
administrative expenses. Management believes that the sales were exempt from
registration under the Securities Act of 1933 (&#147;the Act&#146;) pursuant to Section
4(2) of the Act.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 16px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"><B>ITEM 5.
INDEMNIFICATION OF DIRECTORS AND OFFICERS</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>Although the Company&#146;s
Articles of Incorporation and By Laws do not address the subject of
indemnification, The Idaho Business Corporations Act Sections 30-1-850 through
30-1-859, permits the Company to indemnify its officers and directors against
liabilities they incur in such positions. Pursuant to the Idaho Business
Corporations Act, both permissible and mandatory indemnification is provided for
officers and directors of the Company. </P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>&nbsp;</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 93px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -93px"
align=justify><U>Permissive Indemnification</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 93px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -45px"
align=justify>(1) Except as otherwise provided by law, a corporation may
indemnify an individual who is a party to any threatened, pending or completed
action, suit or proceeding, whether civil, criminal, administrative, arbitrative
or investigative and whether formal or informal (a &#147;Proceeding&#148;) because he is a
director against liability incurred in the proceeding if:</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>(a)
&nbsp;&nbsp;(i) &nbsp;&nbsp;He conducted himself in good faith; and</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 168px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px"
align=justify>(ii) &nbsp;&nbsp;He reasonably believed:</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 192px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>(A)
&nbsp;&nbsp;In the case of conduct in his official capacity, that his</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 240px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px"
align=justify>conduct was in the best interest of the corporation, and </P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>16</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P
style="PADDING-LEFT: 240px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -48px"
align=justify>(B) In all cases, that his conduct was at least not opposed to the
best interests of the corporation; and</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 192px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -48px"
align=justify>(iii) In the case of any criminal proceeding, he had no reasonable
cause to believe his conduct was unlawful; or</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 144px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -48px"
align=justify>(b) He engaged in conduct for which broader indemnification has
been made permissible or obligatory under a provision of the articles of
incorporation, as authorized by section 30-1-202(2)(e), Idaho Code.</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -45px"
align=justify>(2) A director's conduct with respect to an employee plan for a
purpose he reasonably believed to be in the best interests of the participants
in, and the beneficiaries of, the plan is conduct that satisfies the requirement
of subsection (1)(a)(ii)(B) above.</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -45px"
align=justify>(3) The termination of a proceeding by judgment, order, settlement
or conviction, or upon a plea of nolo contendere or its equivalent, is not, of
itself, determinative that the director did not meet the relevant standard of
conduct described in this section.</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -45px"
align=justify>(4) Unless ordered by a court under section 30-1-854(1)(c), Idaho
Code, a corporation may not indemnify a director:</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 144px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -48px"
align=justify>(a) In connection with a proceeding by or in the right of the
corporation, except for reasonable expenses incurred in connection with the
proceeding if it is determined that the director has met the relevant standard
of conduct under subsection (1) of this section; or</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 144px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -48px"
align=justify>(b) In connection with any proceeding with respect to conduct for
which he was adjudged liable on the basis that he received a financial benefit
to which he was not entitled, whether or not involving action in his official
capacity.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -96px"
align=justify><U>Mandatory Indemnification</U> &nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>A corporation shall
indemnify a director who was wholly successful, on the merits or otherwise, in
the defense of any proceeding to which he was a party because he was a director
of the corporation against reasonable expenses incurred by him in connection
with the proceeding.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 96px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -96px"
align=justify><U>Public Policy</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>Insofar as indemnification
for liabilities arising under the Securities Act of 1933 (the "Act") may be
permitted to directors, officers and controlling persons of the small business
issuer pursuant to the foregoing provisions, or otherwise, the small business
issuer has been advised that in the opinion of the Securities and Exchange
Commission such indemnification is against public policy as expressed in the Act
and is, therefore, unenforceable.</P>
<P style="MARGIN-TOP: 14px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 0px"><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>17</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>To the
Board of Directors and</P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px"
align=justify>Stockholders of Superior Silver Mines, Inc.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>We
have audited the accompanying balance sheets of Superior Silver Mines, Inc., (An
Exploration Stage Company) (&#147;the Company&#148;) as of December 31, 2007 and 2006, and
the related statements of operations, changes in stockholders&#146; equity and cash
flows for the years then ended and for the period of exploration stage (January
1, 2007) through December 31, 2007. These financial statements are the
responsibility of the Company&#146;s management. Our responsibility is to express an
opinion on these financial statements based on our audits.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>We
conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the Public Company
Accounting Oversight Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan
and perform the audits to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the
financial statements are free of material misstatement. An audit includes
examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in
the financial statements. An audit also includes assessing the accounting
principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as
evaluating the overall financial statement presentation. We believe that our
audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="PADDING-LEFT: 48px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>In our
opinion, the financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all
material respects, the financial position of Superior Silver Mines, Inc. as of
December 31, 2007 and 2006, and the results of its operations and its cash flows
for the years then ended and for the period of exploration stage (January 1,
2007) through December 31, 2007 in conformity with accounting principles
generally accepted in the United States of America.</P>

<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; MARGIN: 0px"><B>Superior
Silver Mines, Inc.</B></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px"><I>(An Exploration Stage
Company)</I></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px"><B>Notes to Financial Statements</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><B>1. Description of
Business</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>The Company was
incorporated under the laws of the State of Idaho as Superior Mines Company on
January 22, 1962. &nbsp;The Company was established for the purposes of mineral
exploration in the states of Idaho and Montana. &nbsp;In 1964, the Company&#146;s
name was changed to Superior Silver Mines, Inc. &nbsp;The Company has been
dormant for a number of years. &nbsp;It currently holds one unpatented mineral
claim. &nbsp;There are no known mineral reserves on the Company&#146;s property.
&nbsp;Due to the increase in the price of gold, silver and other metals over the
past several years, management is reactivating the Company with the intention of
investigating opportunities in the natural resource industry.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>The Company is an
exploration stage company and has incurred losses since the period of
exploration stage (January 1, 2007). &nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><B>2. Summary of
Significant Accounting Policies</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><U>Exploration Stage
Enterprise</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>The Company&#146;s financial
statements are prepared in accordance with the provisions of Statement of
Financial Accounting Standards No. 7, &#147;Accounting for Development Stage
Enterprises,&#148; as it devotes substantially all its efforts to exploring for
mining interests and developing opportunities that will eventually provide
sufficient net profits to sustain the Company&#146;s existence. &nbsp;Until such
interests and opportunities are engaged in commercial production, the Company
will continue to prepare its financial statements in accordance with entities in
the exploration stage.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><U>Cash and Cash
Equivalents</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>For the purpose of the
balance sheet and statement of cash flows, the Company considers all highly
liquid investments purchased, with an original maturity of three months or less,
to be cash equivalent.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><U>Fair Value of Financial
Instruments</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>The carrying amounts of
financial instruments, including cash and cash equivalents and accounts payable,
approximated their fair values at December 31, 2007 and 2006. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><U>Exploration
Costs</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>Exploration costs are
expensed in the period in which they occur. &nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><U>Use of
Estimates</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>The preparation of
financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted
in the United States of America requires management to make estimates and
assumptions that affect the amounts reported in the financial statements and
accompanying notes. &nbsp;Actual results could differ from those estimates.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=center>24</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>
<HR style="MARGIN-TOP: 9px; MARGIN-BOTTOM: 9px" noShade SIZE=1>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; PAGE-BREAK-BEFORE: always; MARGIN: 0px"
align=justify><B>Superior Silver Mines, Inc.</B></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><I>(An Exploration Stage
Company)</I></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><B>Notes to Financial
Statements</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><B>2. Summary of
Significant Accounting Policies, continued:</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><U>Net Loss Per
Share</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>Such amounts, representing
basic and diluted loss per share, are computed based on the weighted average
number of shares outstanding during the periods December 31, 2007 and 2006.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><U>Income Taxes</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>Income taxes are
recognized in accordance with Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No.
109, &#147;Accounting for Income Taxes,&#148; whereby deferred income tax liabilities or
assets at the end of each period are determined using the tax rate expected to
be in effect when the taxes are actually paid or recovered. &nbsp;A valuation
allowance is recognized on deferred tax assets when it is more likely than not
that some or all of these deferred tax assets will not be realized. &nbsp;The
Company has not recorded an income tax provision, as it has no taxable income.
&nbsp;</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>In June 2006, the FASB
issued Interpretation No. 48, &#147;Accounting for Uncertainty in Income Taxes &#150; an
interpretation of FASB Statement No. 109&#148; (hereinafter "FIN 48"), which
prescribes a recognition threshold and measurement attribute for the financial
statement recognition and measurement of a tax position taken or expected to be
taken in a tax return. FIN 48 also provides guidance on de-recognition,
classification, interest and penalties, accounting in interim periods,
disclosure and transition. The Company adopted FIN 48 on January 1, 2007.
&nbsp;It&#146;s adoption had no effect on the Company&#146;s financial position or results
of operations. </P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><U>Stock Based
Compensation</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>In December 2004, the
Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#147;FASB&#148;) issued SFAS No. 123(R),
&#147;Share-Based Payment.&#148; &nbsp;This Statement is a revision to SFAS No. 123,
&#147;Accounting for Stock-Based Compensation,&#148; and supersedes APB Opinion No. 25,
&#147;Accounting for Stock Issued to Employees&#148; under which guidance the intrinsic
value method was prescribed for awards to employees for services. SFAS No.
123(R) requires the measurement of the cost of employee services received in
exchange for an award of equity instruments based on the grant-date fair value
of the award. The cost will be recognized over the period during which an
employee is required to provide service in exchange for the award. No
compensation cost is recognized for equity instruments for which employees do
not render service.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>The Company adopted SFAS
No. 123(R) using the modified prospective transition method, which requires the
application of the accounting standard as of January 1, 2006. There was no
impact on the financial statements as of and for the year ended December 31,
2006 as a result of the adoption of SFAS No. 123(R). In accordance with the
modified prospective transition method, the financial statements for prior
periods have not been restated to reflect, and do not include, the impact of
SFAS No. 123(R).</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR><BR></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0px"><BR></P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><B>2. Summary of
Significant Accounting Policies, continued:</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><U>Reclamation and
Remediation</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>The Company&#146;s properties
have been and are subject to, standards for mine reclamation that have been
established by various governmental agencies. &nbsp;In June&nbsp;2001, the
Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#147;FASB&#148;) issued SFAS No. 143, &#147;Accounting
for Asset Retirement Obligations&#148;.&nbsp; SFAS 143 requires the Company to record
the fair value of an asset retirement obligation as a liability in the period in
which the Company incurs a legal obligation for the retirement of tangible
long-lived assets.&nbsp; A corresponding asset is also recorded and depreciated
over the life of the asset.&nbsp; After the initial measurement of the asset
retirement obligation, the liability will be adjusted at the end of each
reporting period to reflect changes in the estimated future cash flows
underlying the obligation.&nbsp; Determination of any amounts recognized upon
adoption is based upon numerous estimates and assumptions, including future
retirement costs, future inflation rates and the credit-adjusted risk-free
interest rates. </P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>Environmental costs
relating to properties put into production will be estimated based primarily
upon environmental and regulatory requirements, and are accrued and charged to
expense over the expected economic life of the operation using the
units-of-production method. &nbsp;The liability for reclamation is classified as
current or long-term based on the expected timing of the expenditures.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>The Company accrues costs
associated with environmental remediation obligations when it is probable that
such costs will be incurred and they are reasonably estimable. &nbsp;Such costs
will be based on management&#146;s estimate of amounts expected to be incurred when
remediation work is performed. &nbsp;To date, management is unaware of any
environmental proceedings or action pending against the Company.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><U>Recent Accounting
Pronouncements</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>In September 2006, the
FASB issued Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No. 157, &#147;Fair Value
Measurements,&#148; (hereinafter "SFAS No. 157") which defines fair value,
establishes a framework for measuring fair value in generally accepted
accounting principles (GAAP), and expands disclosures about fair value
measurements. Where applicable, SFAS No. 157 simplifies and codifies related
guidance within GAAP and does not require any new fair value measurements. SFAS
No. 157 is effective for financial statements issued for fiscal years beginning
after November 15, 2007, and interim periods within those fiscal years. Earlier
adoption is encouraged. The Company does not expect the adoption of SFAS No. 157
to have a significant immediate effect on its financial position or results of
operation.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>In December 2007, the FASB
issued SFAS No. 160, &#147;Noncontrolling Interests in Consolidated Financial
Statements &#150; an amendment of ARB 51,&#148; which is effective for fiscal years and
interim periods within those fiscal years, beginning on or after December 15,
2008. &nbsp;SFAS No. 160 amends ARB 51 to establish accounting and reporting
standards for the noncontrolling ownership interest in a subsidiary and for the
deconsolidation of a subsidiary. &nbsp;We are currently evaluating the potential
impact of this statement on our financial statements and at this time we do not
anticipate a material effect.</P>

<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>In December 2007, the FASB
revised SFAS No. 141 &#147;Business Combinations.&#148; &nbsp;The revised standard is
effective for transactions where the acquisition date is on or after the
beginning of the first annual reporting period beginning on or after December
15, 2008. &nbsp;SFAS No. 141(R) will change the accounting for the assets
acquired and liabilities assumed in a business combination.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="PADDING-LEFT: 72px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&nbsp;&nbsp;
Acquisition costs will be generally expenses as incurred;</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="PADDING-LEFT: 72px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183; <FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&nbsp;Noncontrolling
interests (formally known as &#147;minority interests&#148;) will be valued at fair value
at the acquisition date;</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="PADDING-LEFT: 72px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&nbsp; Acquired
contingent liabilities will be recorded at fair value at the acquisition date
and subsequently measured at either the higher of such amount or the amount
determined under existing guidance for nonacquired contingencies;</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="PADDING-LEFT: 72px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&nbsp; In process
research and development will be recorded at fair value as an indefinite lived
intangible asset at the acquisition date;</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="PADDING-LEFT: 72px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183; <FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&nbsp;Restructuring
costs associated with a business combination will be generally expensed
subsequent to the acquisition date; and</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P
style="PADDING-LEFT: 72px; FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px; TEXT-INDENT: -24px; FONT-FAMILY: Symbol"
align=justify>&#183;<FONT style="FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&nbsp; Changes in
deferred tax asset valuation allowances and income tax uncertainties after the
acquisition date generally will affect income tax expense.</FONT></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>The adoption of SFAS No.
141(R) does not currently have a material effect on our financial statements.
&nbsp;However, any future business acquisitions occurring on or after the
beginning of the first annual reporting period beginning on or after December
15, 2008 will be accounted for in accordance with this statement.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>In February 2007, the FASB
issued SFAS No. 159, &#147;The Fair Value Option for Financial Assets and Financial
Liabilities,&#148; which permits entities to choose to measure many financial assets
and financial liabilities at fair value. &nbsp;Unrealized gains on items for
which the fair value option has been elected are to be reported in earnings.
&nbsp;SFAS No. 159 will become effective as of the beginning of the first fiscal
year that begins after November 15, 2007. &nbsp;We do not anticipate the
adoption of SFAS No. 159 to have a material effect on our results of operations
or financial position.</P>

<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px"><B>3. Income Taxes</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>The Company did not record
an income tax provision for the years ended December 31, 2007 and 2006, as it
had no taxable income. At December 31, 2007 and 2006, the Company had net
operating loss carryforwards available for income tax purposes of approximately
$732,000 and $687,000, respectively, which will expire in various amounts from
2008 through 2027. &nbsp;The associated deferred tax asset at December 31, 2007
and 2006 is approximately $293,000 and $275,000, respectively, which was
calculated assuming a 40% marginal combined federal and state income tax rate,
and has been fully reserved as management believes it is more likely than not
that the deferred tax asset will not be utilized. &nbsp;In accordance with
Internal Revenue Code Section 382, pre-2007 net operating loss carryovers will
be limited to approximately $32,000 per year due to the significant ownership
change during the year ended December 31, 2007.</P>

statutory tax rates to pretax income from continuing operations:</P>

shareholders approved a change in the authorized common stock of the Company
from 10,000,000 shares of $0.10 par value common stock to 500,000,000 shares of
$0.0001 par value common stock. &nbsp;The shareholders also approved the
authorization of 10,000,000 shares of $0.0001 par value preferred stock.</P>

<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><U>Private

<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>During December 2006, the
Company sold 552,000 shares of its unregistered common stock for $0.025 per

&nbsp;Proceeds from the offering are expected to be used to fund the Company&#146;s

<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>During July and August
2007, the Company sold 10,325,000 shares of its unregistered common stock for
$0.04 per share. &nbsp;These shares were issued on September 13, 2007 and the
proceeds to the Company from the offering were $360,085. &nbsp;Proceeds from the
offering are expected to be used to fund the Company&#146;s general and
administrative expenses.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>During October 2007, the
Company issued 516,250 shares of its unregistered common stock in connection
with the exercise of warrants at $0.08 per share. &nbsp;The warrants were
granted to a placement agent as compensation for the July and August 2007
private placement. &nbsp;The proceeds to the Company from the exercise were
$41,300, and are expected to be used to fund the Company&#146;s general and
administrative expenses.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><U>Common Stock Issued for
Management and Consulting Services</U></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>On June 27, 2006, the
Company issued 224,000 shares to Thomas S. Smith, the Company&#146;s President, and
224,000 shares to H.F. Magnuson, father of a director of the Company, for
services rendered to the Company. The shares were valued at $0.025 per share
based upon management&#146;s estimate of their fair value at the date of
issuance.</P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><B>5. Related Party
Transactions</B></P>
<P style="MARGIN: 0px" align=justify><BR></P>
<P style="FONT-SIZE: 12pt; MARGIN: 0px" align=justify>In addition to the related
party transactions described in Note 4, at December 31, 2007 and 2006, the
Company owed H.F. Magnuson &amp; Company, a company controlled by H.F. Magnuson,
father of a Director of the Company, $6,570 and $289, respectively for office
expenses. &nbsp;During 2007, the Company paid H.F. Magnuson &amp; Company $2,026
for office expenses.</P>
